title: Observing Enforcement: Evidence from Banking

issues.description: The supplied SAS program creates mod.bnk_vars.sas7bdat from var7_3, while the Stata companion expects a Stata-format bnk_vars in its modified-data working directory. The source chain identifies the consumed bank fields and Stata creates date_stata, yq, RSSDID and Parent_Regulatory_ID_ after load, so a conditional export/conversion with known column-case and path alignment is preparation. The future converted file still needs field/history verification; this is not a separate empirical-data requirement or evidence that a same-basename DTA already exists.
00_build_data.sas includes [redacted-path-76bce5fd35ae] and later invokes %winsor, but that macro is not included in this release. Its definition/version and compatible route are unresolved.

00_build_data.sas reads all_bnk_dist_sas with RSSDID, DATE, REGULATOR and DIST_REG, then logs distance and merges it into the EDO bank-quarter panel. No supplied program produces this table; its source, units, period and bank/regulator matching contract are unresolved.

The SAS code left-joins edo_media_coverage by RSSDID, but no producer or coverage-field definition is supplied. The datasheet describes a hand-collected NewsBank local-media EDO dataset for 1985–1997; obtain the prepared table or its exact construction contract and preserve the authored join.

The SAS news branch reads bnk_vars_county for RSSDID, COUNTY_FIPS, STATE_FIPS and YEAR, but no supplied source constructs this bank-to-county-year mapping. Its population, dates, county assignment and join cardinality remain unresolved; do not assume the separately documented Census urbanization API is this mapping.

The SAS code consumes news_county_8397, derives state_fips/county_fips from cnty90 and uses cov_pct, but no producer for this prepared county-year panel is supplied. The datasheet names ICPSR 30261 and the U.S. Newspaper Panel, but the required subset, county-key mapping, aggregation and field conversion are not documented in this release.

adding_text_analysis.do separately merges edo_complete on rssdid and ISSUE_DATE and then uses EDO_LENGTH. No supplied program produces edo_complete. The SAS input edo_modified (RSSDID/YEAR_QTR/EVENT) is not shown to be the same table or a compatible producer; do not conflate the two names or infer the date/termination mapping.

The old_results_modified keep list and the merged_modified keep list both omit lowercase roa; after appending those data the code executes rename roa roa_text, with no preceding producer visible in the text branch. The later bnk_vars load occurs after this rename. Confirm the intended source field or author correction; do not substitute bank ROA or assume case normalization.

The SAS source uses E: and F: data/output roots; Stata uses a Z: project root and an additional [redacted-path-3a8feb6e0252] path for BEA files. For the host wrapper, stage a working copy under one chosen [redacted-path-9e5595281d32] run root and map all roots/outputs/helper paths coherently while preserving their separate source folders. Actual host visibility/writability and author-drive mapping have not been verified.

evidence.description: README steps 1–7 identify the supplied SAS preparation and Stata companion workflow.
evidence.quote:
/*******************************************************************/
The following steps will replicate the datasets used in the analyses
The steps 1-5 are specified in the code 00_build_data.sas
/*******************************************************************/

Step 1: 
Create the dataset bnk_vars.csv using data from bank call reports. This dataset includes all bank-level variables calculated using the call report data.  

Step 2: 
Include enforcement action data to the main dataset bnk_vars.csv. The enforcement action data is sourced from the SNL financial database for the disclosure period, and hand collected from termination documents and the National Archives for the nondisclosure regime. The data only include severe enforcement actions and only the first enforcement action per bank is retained.

Step 3: 
Clean and merge in data on bank failures downloaded from the FDIC. Include additional identifiers. 

Step 4:
Include data on county-level news circulation downloaded from the Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research. 
The data is the United States Newspaper Panel, 1869-2004 collected by Gentzkow, Shapiro, and Sinkinson (2011).

Step 5: 
Merge hand-collected data on the news coverage of EDOs (collected from the NewsBank archive of local newspapers).

Step 6: 
The regressions are run using Stata. The code adding_emp_growth.do will include the macro variables to the datasets before running the regressions.

evidence.description: The supplied SAS source applies the winsor macro, saves mod.bnk_vars and then reads edo_modified.
The EDO and regulator-distance stages merge supplied bank/EDO inputs and then attach EDO media coverage.
The SAS source creates complete, main-period and robustness-period survival datasets and exports two CSV files.
The SAS source reads FDIC bank failures, joins identifiers from commercial-bank reports and creates a failure panel.
The SAS source reads county assignments and newspaper-panel data, imputes missing county coverage from state means, and saves/exports the result.
The Stata helper imports county BEA data, constructs employment/income growth and saves county_econ in the current directory.

evidence.description: The datasheet identifies SNL and National Archives EDO inputs, FFIEC Call Reports, FDIC failures, BEA CAINC30, NewsBank coverage, ICPSR 30261, and 1990 Census variables.
evidence.quote:
1. We collect all enforcement actions issued by bank regulators disclosed after the in-
     troduction of FIRREA in August 1989 from the S&P Global SNL Financial database.
     To identify enforcement actions in the pre-FIRREA (non-disclosure) period, we mainly
     rely on termination documents that were made public in the post-FIRREA (disclosure)
     period. If a bank received an enforcement order in the pre-FIRREA period, but this
     order was terminated after the passing of the Act, a public termination order reveals
     the identity of the bank that received an enforcement action, as well as the date the en-
     forcement order was originally issued. Initial data for enforcement orders and decisions
     (EDOs) was obtained from SNL Financial. The raw data was first downloaded from
     SNL on February 2, 2018. The corresponding scanned copies of EDOs and termination

                                             1

  orders were received from SNL on March 9, 2018. SNL data was further updated on
  October 4, 2018 and February 18, 2019.

2. We also hand-collected a subset of enforcement actions from the pre-disclosure period
   (1983 and 1984) from the U.S. National Archives. The scanning of the documents took
   place between June 24 and July 3, 2019.

3. We focus our empirical analyses on commercial banks and obtain financial data from
   Call Reports from the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC).
   The initial data was downloaded on April 12, 2018 and updated on May 16, 2018 and
   January 21, 2019.

4. Data on failed banks was downloaded from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
   (FDIC) on December 6, 2018.

5. Recessionary and financial crisis periods were identified using the National Bureau of
   Economic Research (NBER) website.

6. Employment and per capita personal income statistics were downloaded from the Bu-
   reau of Economic Analysis (BEA) on July 16, 2019. The downloaded data-set is
   CAINC30 (Economic Profile by County) and can be found here: https://apps.bea.
   gov/regional/downloadzip.cfm.

7. NewsBank archive data on the coverage of EDO banks by local media was hand-
   collected by a team of undergraduate research assistants and supervised by the research
   professional at Chicago Booth between December 18, 2018 and May 22, 2019. This
   data was collected for 1985–1997.

8. The number of newspaper copies circulated was downloaded from the Inter-university
   Consortium for Political and Social Research (https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/icpsrweb/
   ICPSR/studies/30261). The data is the United States Newspaper Panel, 1869-2004
   collected by Gentzkow, Shapiro, and Sinkinson (2011). The original data came from
   the Editor and Publisher Yearbook (1932-2004). The data was initially downloaded
   on May 22, 2019.

9. Urbanization statistics were collected from the 1990 Decennial Census from the U.S.
   Census Bureau on October 3, 2019. The data was downloaded through the census
   API in Python. The relevant variables are P0060001 (Urban: Inside urbanized area),
   P0060002 (Urban: Outside urbanized area), P0060003 (Rural: Farm), and P0060004
   (Rural: Nonfarm).
